 772–9. Cp. S.’s trans. of Plato, Symposium 195: ‘There were need of some poet like Homer to celebrate
the delicacy and tenderness of Love. For Homer says, that the goddess Calamity is delicate, and that
her feet are tender. “Her feet are soft,” he says, “for she treads not upon the ground, but makes her path
upon the heads of men.” He gives as an evidence of her tenderness, that she walks not upon that which is
hard, but that which is soft. The same evidence is sufficient to make manifest the tenderness of Love. For
